topic: Union-honest rank-and-strength adaptation for a scalar missing-block functional under a public fixed four-block causal-panel mask. Define rank zero separately and exact-rank positive-strength strata. Characterize finite-sample minimax expected length on every stratum under honesty over their union. Decide whether pairwise observed-Gaussian moduli suffice or least-favorable mixtures enlarge the correct functional. Deliver an evaluable characterization and either one data-only q/h-free attaining interval or the sharp unavoidable simultaneous excess. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: a legal 4x4 rank-two signed-permutation mixture has no linear term in chi-square divergence despite positive component KL, and a balanced rank-one analogue suggests an n^(1/4) gap over pairwise modulus. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: simultaneous mixture-test inversion. EARLY KILL TEST: certified solution of the zero-plus-64-orbit interval problem.

open_problems.open_problem: For the fixed four-block Gaussian panel mask, decide whether union-honest expected length for the scalar missing-block functional is governed by pairwise ordered moduli or by a strictly larger least-favorable-mixture modulus, beginning with a certified rank-zero-versus-64-orbit experiment.

source_refs.claim: Between-class and ordered moduli give sharp expected-length lower bounds and constant-factor adaptive intervals for linear functionals over convex Gaussian classes.
source_refs.author: T. Tony Cai and Mark G. Low

source_refs.claim: Sharp expected-length nonadaptivity bounds over nonconvex sparsity classes are obtained by testing a point null against a mixture of alternatives.
source_refs.author: T. Tony Cai and Zijian Guo

source_refs.claim: Honest rank-adaptive matrix confidence sets are controlled by composite low-rank testing difficulty and can be impossible in some observation models.
source_refs.author: Alexandra Carpentier, Olga Klopp, Matthias Loffler, and Richard Nickl

source_refs.excerpt: The signed construction keeps the causal max functional positive while the signs conceal the alternatives
Turn the unknown-rank OEQ into a two-sided testing theorem: state an explicit separation scale

open_problems.why_unsolved: Cai-Low geometry is pairwise and convex-class based, whereas exact-rank strata are nonconvex and their orientations can be randomized. Cai-Guo and Carpentier et al. establish that composite mixtures can be load-bearing, and the prior optimal-value construction shows how sign averaging suppresses low-order distinguishability, but none treats a deterministic causal-panel mask and a scalar target lying in its missing block. The first proof step that changes is the null-mixture likelihood-ratio calculation: it requires the full orbit Gram matrix of masked low-rank alternatives, not the positive KL divergence of each component. The prompt's claimed cancellation and n^(1/4) effect are therefore hypotheses to certify, not established inputs.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A certified finite optimization for the zero-versus-64-orbit affinity and its test inversion, embedded in a formula for the least-favorable prior-mixture modulus, plus a proof that this modulus equals the pairwise modulus or an explicit regime and constant showing strict enlargement and the resulting expected-length lower bound.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation makes the tension between union-wide honesty and subclass expected length the central geometric question.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: honesty is imposed on a large union -> length is evaluated on smaller strata -> pairwise moduli price simple alternatives -> nonconvex rank-orbit mixtures may define a larger obstruction

method_exemplars.technique: Construct a symmetric composite alternative, calculate its null-mixture chi-square affinity from likelihood-ratio cross-moments, and convert indistinguishability into expected-length nonadaptivity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A signed rank orbit has the same fuzzy-hypothesis role, with masked low-rank inner products replacing sparse-support overlaps.

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce honest rank adaptation to composite low-rank testing and turn suitable tests into adaptive confidence procedures.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the rank-testing bridge, while the scalar fixed-mask experiment determines the new testing functional.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate between-class ordered moduli into biased affine estimators, one-sided bounds, and constant-factor expected-length guarantees.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Any mixture replacement must recover the classical pairwise construction when randomization gives no additional affinity.

open_problems.open_problem: Derive the exact finite-sample phase diagram of minimax expected length at rank zero and on every exact-positive-rank stratum indexed by the smallest positive restricted singular value, including its transition to constant length as strength vanishes.

source_refs.claim: Drifting weak-factor regimes change the behavior of principal-components procedures and can make factor-space estimation inconsistent.
source_refs.author: Alexei Onatski

source_refs.claim: Bias-aware panel intervals remain uniformly valid regardless of factor strength, unlike conventional strong-factor intervals.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong, Martin Weidner, and Andrei Zeleneev

source_refs.claim: Entrywise intervals for staggered missing panels attain a nonasymptotic instance-wise lower bound under specified signal and mask conditions.
source_refs.author: Yuling Yan and Martin J. Wainwright

source_refs.excerpt: Replace the binary positive-Gram/no-Gram split with a strength-indexed class whose pre-period Gram may decay
Unknown-rank adaptation remains an open-ended composite-testing question

open_problems.why_unsolved: Weak-factor work establishes regime changes, Yan-Wainwright gives an instance-wise entry benchmark, and the prior SSC reviewer explicitly requests a decay-indexed strength frontier; none yields finite-sample expected length on all exact-rank strata under one union-wide coverage constraint. Rank zero is a singular stratum because factor directions disappear, while near-zero positive-strength alternatives approach it through many orientations. The destination proof must replace the SSC functional-PCR differentiation with the restricted Gaussian observation geometry on each exact-rank tangent cone and must then check whether nonlinear or mixture departures dominate that local calculation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An evaluable piecewise formula L_0 and L_r(s) for every allowed rank r and strength s>0 as functions of the mask, noise law, and sample size, with explicit transition thresholds and matching finite-sample upper and lower bounds or a certified finite optimization computing them.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates uniform inference by showing how weak factors create bias that strong-factor procedures do not price.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: strong factors make low-rank correction appear precise -> weak factors create hidden bias -> validity must hold uniformly in strength -> quantify the exact length price on every rank-strength stratum

method_exemplars.technique: Combine an SVD estimator's finite-sample Gaussian approximation with a Bayesian Cramer-Rao instance-wise lower bound for a missing entry.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It already supplies attainable intervals and local lower benchmarks for a scalar missing-panel target, absent union honesty.

method_exemplars.technique: Use explicit weak-signal PCA expansions and nonasymptotic remainder control to locate the strength threshold at which linearization becomes informative.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired phase diagram is indexed by restricted singular strength and must control failure of factor-space linearization.

method_exemplars.technique: Bound subclass expected length under union coverage using within-class and between-class moduli.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly formalizes the distinction between the rank-strength oracle benchmark and the union-honest benchmark.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether one interval computed only from the observed four blocks and known noise law, with neither rank nor strength inputs, can attain every rank-strength stratum's minimax expected length, and otherwise compute the sharp unavoidable simultaneous excess.

source_refs.claim: Low-rank linear-functional inference can survive an overestimated working rank, but overfitting creates an additional ridge-type bias and still requires a prespecified rank upper bound.
source_refs.author: Jungjun Choi, Hyukjun Kwon, and Yuan Liao
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Debiasing and low-rank projection yield asymptotically normal estimators for matrix linear forms under random noisy matrix completion.
source_refs.author: Dong Xia and Ming Yuan
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: The existence of honest rank-adaptive matrix confidence sets depends on the observation model and on whether noise information is known.
source_refs.author: Alexandra Carpentier, Olga Klopp, Matthias Loffler, and Richard Nickl

source_refs.excerpt: Can one construct a single band without knowing r or the numerical values of the fixed positive lower bounds
Does there exist one sequence ... simultaneously for every t_0>0?

open_problems.why_unsolved: Unknown-rank low-rank procedures either retain a chosen rank upper bound and asymptotic regime or construct full-matrix confidence sets whose diameter is not the scalar expected-length objective. The prior SSC proposal assumes known positive spectral bounds, while its OEQ asks for one band without them; the transported-LATE artifact solves only an analogous scalar weak-ratio problem. Under a deterministic four-block mask, random-completion debiasing starts from an invalid step because the observation operator has a structured null space and the target is wholly missing. Moreover, separately valid oracle intervals cannot simply be selected: simultaneous null-versus-orbit acceptance regions must be made coherent across ranks and strengths.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either an explicit measurable interval based only on observed blocks and the known noise law with finite-sample union coverage and a uniform constant-factor bound relative to every L_r(s), or a theorem giving the exact smallest multiplicative or additive excess that every such interval incurs on at least one stratum.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames unreliable rank selection as the practical inferential obstacle and isolates the bias caused by deliberate overfitting.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: rank selection is unreliable -> inference should survive overfitting -> rank-robust asymptotics still need a working upper rank -> seek a completely rank-and-strength-free honest interval or prove its exact cost

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate low-rank spaces using diversified projections, correct the implicit ridge bias from overfitting, and prove a CLT without consistent rank selection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest constructive route to rank-robust scalar inference, but finite-sample union honesty and removal of the rank upper bound remain open.

method_exemplars.technique: Solve a worst-case bias-variance optimization and invert the bias-aware Gaussian statistic to obtain finite-sample honest intervals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The required interval must price structured missing-block bias, but over a nonconvex union rather than a single convex restriction class.

method_exemplars.technique: Couple low-rank composite tests to oracle confidence sets while proving coverage before data-driven model selection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination likewise requires coherent test inversion across ranks, specialized to a scalar masked functional.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize exactly when the scalar missing-block functional is identifiable under the fixed four-block mask even if the entire low-rank matrix is not uniquely completable, using constancy on full rank-constrained observation fibers rather than tangent directions alone.

source_refs.excerpt: theta_E is identified exactly when every tangent null direction has zero event-time average
Replace the full-injectivity iff for theta_E with a scalar Riesz/annihilator condition

open_problems.why_unsolved: The failed panel proposal isolates scalar recovery as weaker than full-surface injectivity, but its tangent-nullspace condition remained conjectural because nonlinear rank-variety paths can connect points that have no decisive local tangent witness. For the fixed four-block mask, finite expected length is meaningful only on fibers where the target is identified. The first unresolved step is therefore algebraic rather than asymptotic: compute each exact-rank fiber of the observation map and decide target constancy on the entire fiber, then quantify stability on the identifiable quotient.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient fiber-constancy or annihilator criterion for the scalar functional on every exact-rank stratum, an explicit recovery map and quantitative stability constant when it holds, and observationally equivalent rank-constrained counterexamples with separated targets when it fails.

writing_exemplar.why: Its causal-panel setup foregrounds recovery under general intervention masks and naturally separates the causal query from full matrix completion.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: causal panels reveal structured subsets of potential outcomes -> low rank can recover missing counterfactuals under some masks -> full matrix uniqueness is stronger than a scalar causal query needs -> characterize target-specific recovery for the four-block mask

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt observation-subspace and low-rank completion arguments by replacing global injectivity with constancy of the target linear functional on observation fibers.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination is a causal matrix-completion query under a deterministic intervention-shaped missingness pattern.

method_exemplars.technique: Use low-rank debiasing and a target-specific first-order representer after restricting estimation to the identifiable quotient.
method_exemplars.why_closest: If scalar identification holds without full recovery, inference must act through a target representer rather than reconstructing the whole missing surface.

literature_map:
Cai and Low (2004, Annals of Statistics, DOI 10.1214/009053604000000049) characterize adaptive expected length for linear functionals using between-class and ordered moduli.
Cai and Low (2004, Annals of Statistics, DOI 10.1214/009053604000000094) study minimax estimation over finite unions of convex spaces and show nonlinear procedures can be necessary.
Donoho (1994, Annals of Statistics, DOI 10.1214/aos/1176325367) links Gaussian inverse problems, optimal recovery, affine estimation, and functional moduli.
Armstrong and Kolesar (2018, Econometrica, DOI 10.3982/ECTA14434) derive finite-sample bias-aware intervals for linear functionals over convex restriction classes.
Cai and Guo (2017, Annals of Statistics, DOI 10.1214/16-AOS1461) prove expected-length nonadaptivity over sparse unions using composite-mixture tests.
Nickl and van de Geer (2013, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1209.1508) locate an n^(-1/4) honest-adaptation boundary tied to composite testing and separation.
Carpentier, Klopp, Loffler, and Nickl (2018, Bernoulli, arXiv:1608.04861) connect honest rank adaptation in matrix completion to low-rank composite testing.
Athey, Bayati, Doudchenko, Imbens, and Khosravi (2021, JASA, DOI 10.1080/01621459.2021.1891924) establish matrix completion as a causal-panel counterfactual method but focus on estimation rather than union-honest expected length.
Xia and Yuan (2021, JRSSB, DOI 10.1111/rssb.12400) give debiased asymptotic inference for general matrix linear forms under random noisy completion.
Choi and Yuan (2023, arXiv:2308.02364) treat MNAR causal-panel completion with weak signals under asymptotic missing-group conditions.
Yan and Wainwright (2024, arXiv:2401.13665) provide nonasymptotic instance-optimal entrywise intervals for staggered missing panels.
Choi, Kwon, and Liao (arXiv:2311.16440; JASA 2026) avoid consistent rank estimation but retain a prespecified working-rank upper bound and an asymptotic CLT.
Onatski (2009, Econometrica, DOI 10.3982/ECTA6964) and Onatski (2012, Journal of Econometrics, DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2012.01.034) establish weak-factor rank-testing and PCA regime changes.
Fan, Yan, and Zheng (2024, arXiv:2407.03616) develop finite-sample weak-factor inference near minimal strength, while Armstrong, Weidner, and Zeleneev (arXiv:2210.06639; JPE 2026) give factor-strength-uniform bias-aware panel inference.
The unresolved intersection is finite-sample scalar expected length under a deterministic four-block mask: the scan found no result deciding pairwise versus orbit-mixture geometry or solving simultaneous union-honest inversion.
prior_proposal_map:
A repository-wide filename and keyword search covered active, accepted, downgraded, failed, legacy, and _d0_retest_archive paths under CausalSmith/doc/research/**; the active target had only state and pipeline files.
The closest source was _bank/downgraded/stat_ssc_rank_normalization_band_frontier_v1: its README, proto_core, gaps, writeup, and review JSONs were inspected.
That SSC bank entry yielded the unknown-rank OEQ, the angle0_v2 testing strengthening path, and the cold-review directive for a decay-indexed strength frontier with adaptive attainment or impossibility.
For mixture transfer, the README, proto_core, rejected angle, gaps, and reviews for _bank/downgraded/stat_optimal_value_honest_adaptation_finite_action_margin_tie_union were inspected; its signed sparse-mixture construction is the closest fuzzy-hypothesis source.
For scalar rather than full-matrix recovery, the README, proposal and rejected proposals, all reviews, and gaps for _bank/failed/panel_mc_estimation_duality_v1 were inspected; angle4_v2 supplied the scalar Riesz/annihilator correction.
For all-strength inversion, the proto_core, gaps, and angle reviews for _bank/accepted/stat_transported_late_strength_frontier_v1 were inspected.
Additional adjacency checks covered banked spectral HTE, weak-event inference, block-orbit conformal, factor-misspecified synthetic-control, and the active functional-DiD frontier; none produced a more direct fixed-four-block rank-mixture opportunity.
